newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan parties agree on alliance, policy platform.
newsitem.headline: Japan parties agree on alliance, policy platform.

text.p: Parties in Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's outgoing coalition set up a new, loose alliance on Thursday and agreed on a policy platform, including measures to reform the Finance Ministry and other government ministries.

"Things have greatly changed since the coalition under (former prime minister Tomiichi) Murayama," Social Democrat leader Takako Doi said after signing the documents in a meeting with Hashimoto and Akiko Domoto of the Sakigake party.
"The shape of the government will be different. This is what I said during the meeting," Doi said.

Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) failed to win a majority in a general election on October 20 and tried to renew the old coalition, which Hashimoto has been heading since January. But the LDP's two coalition partners, the Social Democrats and Sakigake, refused to take part, fearing they would become irrelevant partners in an LDP-dominated grouping.

Instead, the three parties agreed to keep a loose alliance by setting up policy consultation groups outside the cabinet. The two smaller parties will be excluded from Hashimoto's new cabinet which will be formed on November 7 after his re-election as prime minister. He will head a minority government.

Policy goals include proposed reforms to curtail the power of the Finance Ministry and give more independence to the central bank. Other proposals include reducing the central government's 20 ministries and setting up parliamentary committees to review a controversial planned increase in the sales tax and to oversee the conduct of bureaucrats.
